Gadsden County, Florida Tax Deed Sales: A Complete Guide

If you’re thinking about investing in Gadsden County tax sales, it’s important to understand the process from start to finish. This simple guide will walk you through it.

How Gadsden County Conducts Tax Sales

  • Delinquency Date
    Property taxes become delinquent every year on April 1.
  • Advertising of Delinquent Properties
    Within 45 days, the Tax Collector advertises delinquent properties for three consecutive weeks in a local newspaper. Advertising costs are added to the tax bill.
  • Tax Certificate Sale
    By June 1, Gadsden County will hold a Tax Certificate Sale, typically online through the RealAuction platform.
    Investors bid by offering the lowest interest rate they are willing to accept, starting from a maximum of 18%.
    If the property owner redeems, the investor gets the interest earned.
  • Lien Representation
    Buying a tax certificate does not give ownership of the property. It simply places a lien on the property until the taxes are paid.

Key Information Table

Tax Deed Application Process

  • Eligibility for Application
    After two years from April 1 of the certificate’s issuance, if the taxes are still unpaid, the certificate holder can apply for a Tax Deed.
  • Application Requirements
    • Pay additional amounts (like outstanding taxes and fees).
    • Conduct a title search.
    • Pay application fees.
  • Notification
    The Tax Collector certifies the list of people to be notified and forwards everything to the Clerk of the Circuit Court.

Tax Deed Sale Details

  • Auction Location
    Auctions are now conducted online through RealAuction.
  • Registration
    • Register through RealAuction before the auction.
    • A deposit of $200 or 5% of the anticipated winning bid is required.
  • Auction Time
    Auctions start at 10:00 AM Eastern Time.
  • Winning and Payment
    • The highest bidder wins.
    • Pay a non-refundable deposit immediately (5% or $200, whichever is greater).
    • The remaining balance must be paid quickly after the sale.
  • Payment Methods
    Wire transfers, cashier’s checks, or account transfers from RealAuction.
    No personal checks are accepted.
  • Final Payment Deadlines
    • Wire transfers by 4:00 PM ET on the day of the sale.
    • Deliver cashier’s checks by 9:00 AM ET on the following business day.

Important Notes for Buyers

  • Research Properties Thoroughly
    They sell the Properties as-is. Do a title search and investigate for existing liens or problems.
  • Legal Framework
    Review Chapter 197 of the Florida Statutes and Chapter 12D-13 of the Florida Administrative Code to fully understand tax deed sales.

Why Participate in Gadsden County Tax Sales?

  • Transparent and regulated process.
  • Potential for earning interest up to 18%.
  • Opportunities to acquire real estate at lower prices.
  • Growing interest due to Gadsden’s affordable housing and proximity to Tallahassee.

Contact Information

  • Gadsden County Clerk & Comptroller
    10 E Jefferson Street, Suite 101, Quincy, FL 32351
    Phone: (850) 875-8601
    Email: clerkofcourt@gadsdenclerk.com
    Website: www.gadsdenclerk.com

Interesting Facts About Real Estate in Gadsden County

  • Majority-Black County
    Gadsden County is Florida’s only county with a majority African American population, adding to its unique cultural and historic charm.
  • Affordable Land and Homes
    Land and houses here cost much less than in nearby Leon County (Tallahassee).
  • Strong Rural Living Demand
    There’s high interest in farms, rural homes, and wooded properties.
  • Proximity to Tallahassee
    Many people work in Tallahassee but live in Gadsden for affordable housing.
  • Historic Homes
    Towns like Quincy and Havana have gorgeous historic districts with homes from the 1800s and early 1900s.
